post.caption: This jewelry house began with a wedding. In 1895 in Paris, Estelle Arpels married Alfred Van Cleef. Alfred's father cut stones, and Estelle's father dealt in precious stones. Boucheron was the first jeweler on Place Vendôme, in 1893, and its own first boutique opened there in 1906, at number 22. Estelle's brothers later joined to help run the house. At the 1925 Paris Exposition, the house won a Grand Prix, and in 1933 it patented its Mystery Setting. Its ballerina and fairy clips date from 1941. In 1968, it launched Alhambra, a long necklace of four-leaf clovers.
